records.note: Structural claim in an FDA open comment: clinics that become outpatient distribution centers 'become the distribution channel' for psychedelic medicines. No drug, REMS document, deciding body, series or threshold is named, and the sentence continues into the normative point about economic viability. 'These medicines' is the psychedelic class, but 'distribution channel' has no observable resolution without inventing a dispensing-site criterion. No confidence words and no time words.

Adequacy judgment: the existing Category III psychedelic-therapy CPT codes cap monitoring at 6 hours, which 'may not be enough' for the REMS programs FDA is considering for 'some of these compounds'. No compound, REMS document or monitoring threshold beyond the existing 6-hour cap is named, and 'some of these compounds' has no countable set. The claim judges whether a code fits programs FDA has not published; no third-party decision is asserted. 'May' would be bin C if admitted. No time words.

'The REMS program will drive the reimbursement infrastructure' is a causal claim with no observable event: no REMS document, code, payer or threshold is named, and 'drive' has no benchmark. The second sentence of the extraction (a new code set 'will almost certainly need to be the case') is the same text as owen-2367 and is coded there, so this row is not a DUPLICATE. 'Will' would be bin A if admitted. No time words.

Necessity claim: a 'robust new code set' 'will almost certainly need to be the case' to encompass 'all the psychedelic treatments that are coming'. The words predict a need, not a decision: no code-setting body (AMA CPT Editorial Panel or CMS), code category or effective date is named, 'robust new code set' has no observable threshold, and 'all the psychedelic treatments that are coming' has no countable set. Same test as the 'physicians will be needed' call in an earlier packet (owen-1085); the normative frame ('need to') is also present. 'Will almost certainly' would be bin A if admitted. 'Are coming' is not a deadline.

'Will need complexity based billing and longer monitoring' for nearly every late-stage psychedelic: a necessity claim about clinical and billing practice, not a third-party decision. No REMS document, code, payer or monitoring threshold is named; 'longer' is a comparative whose benchmark (ketamine and esketamine monitoring) is not tied to any deciding body's observable action, and 'and more' leaves the set open. Restates the longer-monitoring call. 'Will' would be bin A if admitted. No time words.

Hypothetical evaluation: it 'would be commercially and clinically disastrous' to have approved medicines with no plausible clinic reimbursement. 'Disastrous' has no benchmark, series or threshold, and the condition (approval with 'no plausible means of reimbursement') is not observable. A warning inside a recommendation to FDA, not a forecast of a third-party decision.

'Is itself an access barrier measured in years' describes the consequence of post-approval payer-by-payer rate negotiation. No access metric, series, threshold or payer is named, and 'measured in years' is a magnitude, not a deadline. Present-tense characterization inside Recommendation 3.

'Buy-and-bill ... is likely to be necessary' predicts a need, not a decision: no drug, payer, code or REMS document is named, and the sentence is a recommendation to FDA about which codes to use. Whether buy-and-bill 'is necessary' has no resolution source. 'Likely' would be bin B if admitted. No time words.
'Likely to be expensive drugs': no drug, price threshold, comparator or series is named. A comparative without a benchmark. 'Likely' would be bin B if admitted.

'These drugs are likely to rise in price': the drugs are unnamed psychedelics with no named product or list price in the quote, and no price series, threshold or period is named, so no quantity event can be written. Embedded in a recommendation about a drug price multiplier. 'Likely' would be bin B if admitted.

'Coverage decisions will require economic data on the cost utility of these compounds': a claim about payers' evidence requirements, with no payer, program, compound or coverage decision named. TCET and the Breakthrough Treatments Act appear in the context as comparators, not as the object of a forecast. 'Will' would be bin A if admitted. No time words.

Conditional consequence built on the esketamine analogy: a slow commercial ramp 'would undercut financial support ... in the minds of financial markets, thus limiting future innovation'. No company, series, threshold or period; 'financial support' and 'innovation' have no benchmark, and the condition (psychedelics repeat esketamine's ramp) is itself unmeasured.

'What is acceptable according to Medicare is likely to be followed by other payors': no Medicare policy exists in the quote to be followed, no payer, standard or date is named, and 'other payors' has no countable set. 'Likely' would be bin B if admitted. No time words.

Hedged claim that 'teams of Psychiatrist and other health professionals ... may be involved in the dispensing' of psychedelics. No REMS document, prescriber definition, deciding body or threshold is named; the sentence argues for how FDA should define prescribers. 'May' would be bin C if admitted.

List of what a psychedelic-capable clinic 'will require' (per-patient rooms, monitoring staff, secure storage, audiovisual and IT infrastructure). A requirements description, not a third-party decision: no REMS document, DEA rule or deciding body's action is named and none of the items has a threshold. 'Will' would be bin A if admitted.

Conditional: if reimbursement ignores clinic costs, 'the only entities able to observe the losses will be large, vertically, integrated organizations'. Neither the condition (reimbursement 'does not count' clinic costs) nor the consequent (which entities absorb losses) has a series, threshold or countable set. 'Will' would be bin A if admitted.
'Set and setting are likely to be crucial factors of the deployment': 'crucial' has no benchmark, and no observable event or deciding body is named. 'Likely' would be bin B if admitted.

Psychedelics 'rolled out without concern for the underlying economics, could make [market consolidation] more common place'. Conditional on an unmeasured rollout condition; 'more common place' is a quantifier with no countable set, series or threshold. 'Could' would be bin C if admitted.

Conditional: if independent practices cannot deliver at payer rates without losing money, 'access will narrow'. The condition is not observable as stated (no payer, rate or practice set) and 'access will narrow' names no metric, series or threshold. 'Regardless of how many products the FDA approves' asserts no approval count. 'Will' would be bin A if admitted.

Argument to FDA: blanket in-person requirements 'would function as a geographic access restriction without a corresponding safety benefit'. A hypothetical evaluation of a requirement FDA has not issued; no access metric, safety metric, threshold or decision is named.

'A class of medicines cannot reach patients without clinicians and clinical infrastructure in the loop': a structural description of the psychedelic class, with no drug, REMS document, deciding body or threshold. Same test as the 'physicians will be needed' call in an earlier packet (owen-1085). 'For the first time in psychiatry' is retrospective framing. No confidence words and no time words.

Denial: the psychedelic class 'will not use' the 'rebate-driven pharmacy-benefit model'. The payment-model characterization has no single resolution source: rebates are confidential, pharmacy-benefit versus medical-benefit status is set payer by payer and drug by drug, and no drug, payer or period is named. A coder could map the claim to REMS dispensing restrictions (the REMS event proposed in an earlier packet, owen-1086), but a REMS that limits dispensing to certified settings does not determine the benefit under which the drug is paid, so that mapping would change the proposition. 'Will not' would be bin A with asserts false (p(E) = 0.10) if admitted. 'Anyway' is not a deadline.

'The questions that will determine whether approved psychedelic therapies reach the patients': a causal claim about what decides access, with no metric, series, threshold or decision named. 'Reach the patients' has no benchmark. 'Will' would be bin A if admitted.

Own-event announcement: the author organizes RAMHT and announces its next live event for 14 September 2026 in New Orleans. Whether the event happens is the forecaster's own decision. Also outside the five areas.

Social prediction that a Radial technician would be invited back to the Soft White Underbelly YouTube channel. A media invitation is not a regulatory, trial, company or market, payer or policy, or practice-adoption outcome. 'I'm sure' reads as an A phrase ('certain') if a forecast in area were present; 'would be welcome back' names no invitation or date.

Own-event announcement: RAMHT New Orleans on 14 September 2026, sponsored by the author's companies Neurolief and Radial. The forecaster's organization decides whether the event happens. 'Is coming up' is a schedule statement, not a forecast.
Own-activity promise: RAMHT (the author's event series) will share speaker and program details on its website and LinkedIn page. The forecaster's own organization decides.
Own-event detail: RAMHT New Orleans 'will have special guests. And surprises.' The organizer decides the program; 'special guests' and 'surprises' also have no countable set.

Own-event detail: the RAMHT New Orleans event 'maybe' includes merchandise embarrassing to the author. The organizer decides; the playful hedge changes nothing. CONTROL rather than SATIRE because the finder reads it as a real hedge and the own-organization test is met first.

Efficacy belief: accelerated TMS, 'particularly the SNT approach', 'is likely to work' in bipolar depression. No trial, sponsor, endpoint or effect-size threshold is named, so a trial_result event would require inventing a trial; 'work' has no benchmark, unlike the 'demonstrate statistical significance' wording admitted in an earlier packet (owen-0070-a). The same test rejected 'might work' for accelerated TMS in adolescent depression (owen-1947). The 'large enough trial, submitted to the FDA' clause states a necessary step, not a predicted trial or label decision, and is coded at owen-2395. 'Likely' would be bin B if admitted. Earlier packets note that the author's employer Radial offers SAINT-type accelerated TMS, so the item would be affiliated if it were admitted. No time words.

Describes the pathway to an FDA label change for accelerated TMS in bipolar depression: 'somebody has to do a large enough trial, submitted to the FDA', and a label change 'just starts the conversation with payers'. 'Has to' states a regulatory necessity; no trial, sponsor, submission, label decision or payer decision is asserted to occur, so no future state is forecast. A coder reading a prediction that coverage lags any label would still have no payer, policy or benchmark, and no time words.

Negative coverage call: the KET-BD randomized data are 'unlikely to lead to meaningful coverage' of IV ketamine for bipolar depression. The drug, indication and outcome type are clear, but 'meaningful coverage' is a quantifier with no countable set of payers, and no payer, program (a Medicare NCD or LCD, a named commercial policy), policy or period is named, so a coverage_decision event would require inventing the payer and the threshold. Earlier payer items were admitted only when the payer and program were named (Medicare NTAP, owen-0529 and owen-0796-b). 'Unlikely' would set bin D, asserts true (p(E) = 0.30), if admitted. No time words.

Structural market claim: bipolar depression is 'more of an unmeetable need' because the founder who pitches a market '5x bigger' 'wins, all things being equal'. No company, program, trial count, series or threshold; 'unmeetable need' and 'wins' have no benchmark, and no period is named. Reads as a present-tense generalization; the forward-looking reading (bipolar-specific development stays scarce) has no countable set.

'This will be less true financially than it will be emotionally': a soft claim about the return on a bipolar-focused company, with no company, return metric, series or threshold. 'Will' would be bin A if admitted.

Own-voice endorsement of Randy Pardell's forecast that 'we'll be questioning why we ever did this with SSRIs'. Not THIRD_PARTY: the author adopts it as his own ('to your point'). No observable event: who questions, in which guideline, label, series or decision, and by when, is not stated. The author discloses that he advises Outro Health, which would make the item affiliated if an event naming Outro were admitted. 'We'll be' would be bin A if admitted.

Retrospective generalization in a question to Randy Pardell: 'Every time TMS has been evaluated, eventually it's determined that this is a great option'. Describes a past pattern; the forward-looking reading is the finder's inference, and 'more people should have access' is normative. 'Eventually' is not a deadline, and no payer, evaluation or decision is named. Same test as the habitual conversion-factor description in an earlier packet (owen-1202).

Fundraising call to action: a donation to FACTMS 'means more people get access to TMS treatment at a lower cost ... and there'll be more research'. 'More people', 'lower cost' and 'more research' are quantifiers and comparatives with no countable set, series or benchmark, and the consequent is conditional on donations the author is soliciting. 'There'll be' would be bin A if admitted.
Own-newsletter content promise: a multi-part article on the Lindsay Clancy case is 'coming up soon' in The Frontier Psychiatrists. The author's own action. 'Soon' is not a deadline.

Own-newsletter and own-event promise: coverage of RAMHT New Orleans (the author's event series) on 14 September 2026. The author's own action, as with earlier 'more coverage coming' promises (owen-1155, owen-1168).

States that a psychedelic open comment period falls on 14 September 2026, the same day as RAMHT New Orleans. A calendar fact passed on as information ('There is'), not an expectation: no agency, docket or outcome is named and nothing uncertain is asserted. Same test as the DEA comment-period statement in an earlier packet (owen-0329); a coder who reads it as a schedule already announced by the deciding body would code KNOWN.
